overall: Los Angeles reached its daily peak of 75.2°F at approximately 15:34 ET (roughly 12:34 PT), well above the NWS Tuesday forecast of 72°F. Temperatures have been cooling steadily since, now sitting at 69.8°F with a velocity of -1.8°F/hr, meaning the day's high is effectively locked in. The pattern ran warmer than most official guidance anticipated, driven by a southerly flow and clear skies through the afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: There was notable model spread today — GFS (74.1°F) and HRRR (74.6°F) tracked much closer to observed reality, while ECMWF (70.2°F) and NBM (70.2°F) underforecast by roughly 5°F. The NWS official narrative of 72°F also undershot significantly. GFS and HRRR were the clear winners in today's model competition.
max_temp_prediction: With the peak already confirmed at 75.2°F roughly 6 hours ago and a strong cooling trend underway (-1.8°F/hr), today's TMAX is essentially final. The META model (86.7%) and INTRADAY model (95.8%) both overwhelmingly favor the 74-75F even bucket, which is consistent with a 75.2°F observed maximum. Confidence is very high — this is a near-certain outcome for the 74-75F Kalshi even bucket.
